breakfast.name: Eggs Benedict
ingredients: Hollandaise: 3 egg yolks, 150g butter (clarified), lemon juice, cayenne, salt
instructions: Make hollandaise: whisk yolks over double boiler, slowly drizzle in clarified butter, add lemon juice, cayenne, salt
Fry back bacon until lightly browned
Poach eggs: bring water to gentle simmer with vinegar, swirl, slip eggs in, cook 3 min
Toast muffin halves
Stack: muffin, bacon, poached egg
Spoon hollandaise over — it should be thick enough to coat but still flow
breakfast.description: A dish with strong Canadian roots — back bacon instead of ham is the Canadian hallmark. Weekend brunch across the country.

breakfast.name: Crêpes au Sirop d'Érable (Maple Syrup Crêpes)
instructions: Whisk flour, eggs, milk, melted butter, salt into thin batter
Rest 10 min
Heat buttered crêpe pan, pour thin layer of batter
Cook until edges lift, flip, cook 30 sec more
Stack crêpes, drizzle generously with maple syrup
Top with whipped cream and berries
breakfast.description: Thin French-Canadian crêpes swimming in Quebec maple syrup — the sweetest breakfast in the country.

breakfast.name: Bannock
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, salt, sugar
Cut in butter until crumbly
Add water, stir to form soft dough — don't overwork
Shape into rounds or one large flat disc
Bake at 190°C for 20-25 min, or fry in oil until golden on both sides
Serve warm with butter, jam, or honey
breakfast.description: Indigenous bread — made for centuries by First Nations peoples across Canada. Baked or fried, always warm, always shared.

lunch.name: Poutine
ingredients: Gravy: 2 cups beef stock, 2 tbsp butter, 2 tbsp flour, pepper, salt
instructions: Cut potatoes into thick fries, soak in cold water 30 min, dry thoroughly
Fry at 150°C for 5 min (blanch), drain, fry again at 190°C until golden and crispy
Make gravy: melt butter, whisk in flour, cook 2 min, add stock, simmer until thickened
Place hot fries in bowl
Scatter cheese curds — they MUST be room temperature and squeaky
Ladle hot gravy over — it partially melts the curds
Eat immediately — poutine waits for no one
lunch.description: Quebec's gift to the world — crispy fries, squeaky cheese curds, hot gravy. The curds must squeak when you bite them; that's how you know they're fresh.

lunch.name: Montreal Smoked Meat Sandwich
instructions: The brisket has been cured with salt, pepper, coriander, garlic for 10 days, then smoked
Steam the smoked meat for 3-4 hours until incredibly tender
Slice by hand — thick or thin, your call (medium is classic)
Pile high on rye bread — at least 200g per sandwich
Add yellow mustard only — nothing else
Serve with a full dill pickle on the side
lunch.description: Montreal's answer to the deli sandwich — peppery, smoky brisket piled on rye. Schwartz's has served them since 1928.

lunch.name: Tourtière (Meat Pie)
ingredients: Pastry: 500g flour, 250g butter or lard, cold water, salt
Filling: 500g ground pork, 250g ground veal, 1 onion, 2 potatoes (diced small), cinnamon, cloves, allspice, sage, salt, pepper, 200ml beef broth
instructions: Make pastry: cut butter into flour and salt, add cold water, form dough, chill 30 min
Sauté onion, add meats, brown, break up
Add diced potato, spices, broth
Simmer until potato is tender and liquid absorbed — filling should be moist but not wet
Cool filling
Line pie dish with pastry, fill, top with pastry lid, crimp edges, cut steam vents
Bake at 200°C for 35-40 min until golden
lunch.description: French-Canadian meat pie — mandatory at Christmas Eve réveillon. Every Québécois family guards their spice ratio.

dinner.name: Butter Tart-Glazed Salmon
ingredients: Glaze: 2 tbsp butter, 3 tbsp maple syrup, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp Dijon mustard, lemon juice
instructions: Season salmon with salt and pepper
Make glaze: melt butter, whisk in maple syrup, soy, mustard, lemon
Sear salmon skin-side down in hot pan 4 min
Flip, brush with glaze
Finish in 200°C oven for 8-10 min, brushing glaze twice more
Garnish with dill
dinner.description: Pacific or Atlantic salmon with a maple-mustard glaze — Canada's two coasts meet in one dish.

dinner.name: Alberta Beef Stew
instructions: Toss beef in flour, brown in batches in hot oil
Sauté onion and garlic
Add tomato paste, cook 2 min
Deglaze with stout
Add broth, thyme, bay leaf, return beef
Simmer covered 60 min
Add potatoes, carrots, parsnips
Cook 45 more min until everything is falling-apart tender
Season generously
dinner.description: Hearty prairie stew — Alberta beef slow-cooked with root vegetables and stout. Made for cold Canadian winters.

dinner.name: Jiggs Dinner
ingredients: 1 salt beef pudding bag or pease pudding (split yellow peas in cheesecloth)
instructions: Simmer salt beef in fresh water for 2 hours
Add turnip and pease pudding bag, cook 30 min
Add carrots and potatoes, cook 20 min
Add cabbage, cook 15 min
Everything cooks in the same pot in stages
Serve on a big platter with drawn butter on the side
The pease pudding is mashed and served alongside
dinner.description: Newfoundland's Sunday dinner — salt beef boiled with root vegetables. The whole island smells of it on Sunday afternoon.

snacks.name: BeaverTails (Fried Pastry)
ingredients: Toppings: cinnamon sugar, Nutella, maple butter, lemon and sugar
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, salt, sugar
Cut in butter, add milk, form dough
Divide into balls, stretch each into a long flat oval (beaver tail shape)
Deep fry 1-2 min per side until golden and puffy
Top with cinnamon sugar (classic) or other toppings
snacks.description: Flat fried pastry stretched into a beaver-tail shape — an Ottawa original, sold at every winter festival and skating rink.

snacks.name: Nanaimo Bars
ingredients: Base: 1/2 cup butter, 1/4 cup sugar, 5 tbsp cocoa, 1 egg, 2 cups graham crumbs, 1 cup coconut, 1/2 cup walnuts
Middle: 1/4 cup butter, 2 tbsp custard powder, 2 cups powdered sugar, 3 tbsp cream
instructions: Base: melt butter with sugar and cocoa over double boiler, add egg, stir until thick, mix in crumbs, coconut, walnuts, press into 9x9 pan
Chill 10 min
Middle: cream butter, custard powder, sugar, cream until fluffy, spread over base
Chill 10 min
Top: melt chocolate with butter, spread over middle layer
Chill until set, cut into bars
snacks.description: Three-layer no-bake bars from Nanaimo, BC — chocolate crumb, custard cream, chocolate ganache. No Canadian bake sale is complete without them.

snacks.name: Poutine (Fries, Cheese Curds, Gravy)
ingredients: Rich gravy: beef stock, butter, flour, pepper, splash of vinegar
instructions: Cut potatoes into thick fries, soak in cold water 30 min, dry thoroughly
Fry at 150°C for 5 min (blanch), rest, then fry at 190°C until golden and crispy
Make gravy: melt butter, whisk in flour, add hot beef stock, season, simmer until thick
Cheese curds must be at room temperature — cold curds won't melt right
Layer: hot fries, then curds (the heat starts melting them), then hot gravy over everything
The curds should be squeaky and half-melted — fully melted is wrong, unmelted is wrong
Eat immediately — poutine waits for no one
snacks.description: Quebec's gift to the world — the unholy trinity of crispy fries, squeaky cheese curds, and hot gravy. The cheese must squeak when you bite it. Viral poutine debates (is it just cheesy fries? No.) and extreme poutine variations are a permanent fixture of food internet.

desserts.name: Butter Tarts
ingredients: Pastry: 250g flour, 150g cold butter, pinch salt, cold water
Filling: 1 cup brown sugar, 1/2 cup corn syrup, 2 eggs, 2 tbsp butter (melted), 1 tsp vanilla, 1 tsp vinegar, pinch salt
Raisins or pecans (optional — this is a contentious issue)
instructions: Make pastry, chill 30 min, roll, cut rounds, line tart pans
Mix filling: whisk brown sugar, corn syrup, eggs, melted butter, vanilla, vinegar, salt
Add raisins or pecans if you dare (or leave plain — Canadians argue about this)
Fill tart shells two-thirds full
Bake at 230°C for 12-15 min until pastry is golden and filling is set but still slightly wobbly in the center
Cool — the filling firms as it cools
desserts.description: The great Canadian pastry — gooey brown sugar filling in flaky pastry. Raisins or no raisins divides the nation more than politics.

desserts.name: Pouding Chômeur (Poor Man's Pudding)
ingredients: Cake: 1 cup flour, 1 tsp baking powder, 1/4 cup butter, 1/2 cup sugar, 1 egg, 1/2 cup milk, vanilla
Sauce: 1.5 cups maple syrup, 1 cup cream
instructions: Make cake batter: cream butter and sugar, add egg, alternate flour with milk
Pour batter into greased baking dish
Heat maple syrup and cream together — do NOT mix into batter
Pour hot syrup-cream mixture OVER the batter gently
Bake at 175°C for 30-35 min — the cake rises through the sauce
The sauce ends up on the bottom, the cake on top
Serve warm, spooning sauce from the bottom over each portion
desserts.description: Depression-era Quebec dessert — cake batter baked in maple cream sauce. It inverts itself in the oven. Impossibly rich and humble at the same time.

desserts.name: Nanaimo Bars (No-Bake Layered Bars)
ingredients: Base: 1/2 cup butter, 1/4 cup sugar, 5 tbsp cocoa, 1 egg, 2 cups graham cracker crumbs, 1 cup coconut, 1/2 cup walnuts
Middle: 1/4 cup butter, 2 cups icing sugar, 2 tbsp custard powder, 3 tbsp cream
Top: 4 oz semi-sweet chocolate, 2 tbsp butter
instructions: Base: melt butter, sugar, cocoa over double boiler, stir in egg, add crumbs, coconut, walnuts, press into 9x9 pan, chill
Middle: cream butter, add icing sugar, custard powder, cream — spread over base, chill
Top: melt chocolate and butter, spread over middle layer, chill until set but not hard
Score into bars while chocolate is slightly soft
Refrigerate until firm, cut into bars
Named after Nanaimo, British Columbia — every Canadian has an opinion about the best version
desserts.description: A no-bake three-layer bar from Nanaimo, BC — chocolate-coconut-nut base, custard buttercream middle, chocolate ganache top. The cross-section reveal videos are perpetually viral, and the 'is it a cookie or a dessert' debate never ends.

drinks.name: Caesar (Canadian Cocktail)
ingredients: Garnish: celery stalk, pickle, bacon, whatever you like
instructions: Rim glass with celery salt and lime
Fill with ice
Add vodka, hot sauce, Worcestershire
Fill with Clamato juice
Stir gently
Garnish with celery stalk — or go wild with pickles, bacon, shrimp, a whole burger (yes, this happens)
drinks.description: Canada's national cocktail — invented in Calgary in 1969. Like a Bloody Mary but with clam-tomato juice. Canadians drink 400 million a year.

drinks.name: Caribou (Hot Wine Punch)
instructions: Heat wine with spices and orange peel — do not boil
Add maple syrup
Add rye whisky off heat
Serve hot in mugs
drinks.description: Quebec's winter warmer — red wine, rye whisky, and maple syrup. Served at Quebec City's Carnaval from communal canes. Dangerously good in the cold.
